subject: T423: multi-model whole-Bible chunking fork (experimental)
summary: Logos-scripture-graph is trying a speed fork: 4-5 AI models each run a continuous whole-Bible chunking marathon in separate scratch folders (M1_cursor..M5_composer_alt), starting from the same research baseline (literature types, grammar, Strong's G/H, wj/red-letter, observation substrate). After marathons: agreement spans = easy/consensus chunks; disagreement delta = governed focus queue. If fork fails, revert to T410 parallel_chunking_research_program baseline. Red-team pre-mortem required before marathons.

subject: Request: independent red-team pre-mortem of T423 fork
summary: Before any whole-Bible marathon starts, an independent AI should run .ai/prompts/multi_model_whole_bible_chunking_redteam_premortem_prompt.md and write .ai/scratch/multi_model_bible_chunking/redteam/REDTEAM_PREMORTEM_REPORT.md with GO/HOLD/ABANDON_FORK verdict.

subject: T450: Bible edge taxonomy lanes before graph generation
summary: Logos Scripture Graph is defining planning-only edge-family lanes before any production graph work: structural/source occurrence, editorial metadata, intertext, prophecy/apocalyptic, orthodox creedal theology, covenant, sacrifice/temple/priesthood, literary/discourse/genre, chronology/calendar/geography, linguistic/original-language, manuscript/textual witness, historical/cultural/reception, and apologetic/polemic. The reusable lesson is to separate deterministic edges from reviewed semantic/theological claims and model-inferred candidates before allowing any edge database buildout.
extra_context: The owner wants many models to help identify all Bible-appropriate edge types for apologetic, polemic, theological, linguistic, historical, prophetic, calendar, sacrifice, covenant, wisdom, Daniel/Revelation, and literary/hermeneutic uses. The local repo must avoid covert liberal-critical defaults, covert denominational system selection, and model-generated theology authority. Strong's, WJ/red-letter, editorial crossrefs, headings, footnotes, manuscript age, and model agreement are evidence only. High-risk lanes require frontier review and owner gate before predicate registry expansion or graph edge generation.

subject: DAD central repo dirty during parallel Rust rollouts
summary: The DAD repo was itself very dirty while multiple repos are deploying Rust and reporting lessons back to DAD. This is expected to become common: many repos will consult DAD, append candidate lessons, and report Rust/tooling failures in parallel. DAD likely needs a dirty-state-safe intake design rather than expecting agents to clean the central repo.
extra_context: Observed operating rule from Logos Scripture Graph: 'The DAD repo is itself very dirty with an active Rust rollout, so I am going to be careful: read the mail format, then append one candidate-only message if the format is straightforward. I will not try to clean up DAD or touch unrelated Rust rollout files.' The owner wants coding agents across repos to report DAD/tool errors in a categorized way, with enough extra context for DAD to learn why the error happened and whether it should become a future exception-lake case. Requirements should include a minimum structured set plus an extra_context area for messy real-world context.
possible_fixes: append-only mail spool with atomic writes
dirty-state preflight with categorized environment-noise reporting
lock or claim files for DAD maintenance tasks
exception lake for repeated tool/path/install failures
central collector that normalizes candidate messages after intake
documented rule that source repos may append candidate mail but may not clean DAD
extra_context field in future DAD requirement schemas

subject: T424: Rust fast validators and Rust-first coding runtime preflight
summary: T424 adds an isolated Rust fast-validator CLI, Python wrappers with fallback, and a coding runtime preflight that requires Rust consideration for high-resource deterministic validators/scanners/importers/chunk-map comparisons/CI hot paths. Candidate DAD assets are the Rust leaf-validator pattern, Rust-first preflight thresholds, and Python-wrapper/Rust-fallback pattern. Local repo authority remains unchanged.
lesson_summary: Use Rust for deterministic high-resource scans when runtime/data-size thresholds make it worthwhile; keep Python/pytest as governance orchestrator and record interop, fallback, validation, maintenance, and authority tradeoffs.

subject: T424-D lesson candidate: Rust chunk-map validation as leaf check, not comparison authority
summary: A good Rust slice for large AI scratch outputs is a deterministic chunk-map leaf validator that checks required fields, non_authorizing flags, model-id scope, canonical book scope, span shape, duplicate decision ids, contiguous per-book indices, overlap/order, and optional full-Bible book coverage. Python should keep model comparison, agreement/delta policy, stress-book handling, frontier escalation, owner gates, and promotion decisions.
extra_context: This refinement came from the T423 multi-model whole-Bible chunking fork. It is useful because many independent AI model marathons can produce large scratch chunk maps; Rust can cheaply validate structural safety before Python performs governance-heavy comparison. The lesson does not make scratch chunks canon, does not promote agreement chunks, and does not authorize route/evaluator behavior.

lesson_candidate.pattern: Rust leaf validator for large AI scratch chunk maps; Python retains comparison and promotion policy
lesson_candidate.use_when: Multiple AI agents/models produce large JSONL chunk maps that need deterministic field/span/coverage checks before governed comparison.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: The task is deciding chunk quality, easy/agreement promotion, reviewed gold, theological risk, or route/evaluator behavior.

subject: T423/T424 lesson candidate: complete progress status must not imply aggregate artifact presence
summary: A read-only T424-D real-data check found one model slot marked complete with 66 per-book chunk files but no merged whole_bible_chunk_map.jsonl, while another complete model had the merged map and passed Rust/Python parity. Reusable lesson: orchestration should validate required aggregate artifacts independently from progress/status flags; per-book artifacts can pass while the merged comparison input is still absent.
extra_context: The Rust leaf validator checked explicit scratch artifacts only: M4's merged map passed with 1,319 records, and 156 per-book chunk files across visible model slots passed. No comparison or promotion ran. This is a DAD orchestration lesson about artifact completeness, not a judgment about chunk quality.

lesson_candidate.pattern: status flag plus per-item outputs are insufficient; validate required aggregate artifact presence before downstream comparison
lesson_candidate.use_when: Parallel AI/model workers save per-book or per-unit outputs and a later comparison/integration stage expects a merged aggregate file.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: The pipeline has no aggregate downstream consumer or the aggregate is intentionally deferred and explicitly represented as absent.

subject: T425 lesson candidate: DAD outbox references must have local lesson and context slots
summary: T425 hardens DAD reporting so an outbox row that advertises a lesson_learned_slot or context_map_entry must point at an existing local artifact with matching task id, message id, trust zone, local adoption flag, extra context, and non-authorizations. This prevents dirty parallel repo work from creating dangling DAD lesson references.
extra_context: This was prompted by parallel Rust rollout work across repos and the owner requirement that DAD receive useful messy context without agents trying to clean unrelated DAD checkout state. The local source repo now leaves auditable slots for DAD to ingest later, while preserving DAD as candidate-only and local governance as authoritative.

lesson_candidate.pattern: DAD outbox lesson/context references fail closed unless local auditable slots exist and agree with the message
lesson_candidate.use_when: A repo reports candidate lessons/assets to DAD during dirty parallel work, Rust rollout, tooling failures, or cross-repo asset reuse.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: The message is a one-off notification with no reusable lesson slot or context-map entry.

subject: T456 lesson candidate: sandbox temp and Cargo routing before runtime verdicts
summary: Logos Scripture Graph is hardening test runtime preflight after Windows/Codex sandbox runs hit access-denied failures around pytest temp/cache paths, Python TemporaryDirectory outputs, and Cargo target/build locks. The reusable lesson is to route pytest basetemp, TMP/TEMP, and CARGO_TARGET_DIR to writable repo-local ignored paths before interpreting failures, and to distinguish sandbox environment noise from real code or data failures.
extra_context: The owner expects many repos to deploy Rust validators and report lessons to DAD in parallel. These repos will frequently have dirty worktrees, sandboxed shells, and long-running validation gates. DAD should provide a reusable runtime-environment preflight asset with minimum structured fields and an extra_context area so messy observations like WinError 5, Cargo lock denial, temp-dir denial, rerun context, and whether the failure reproduced unsandboxed are preserved without forcing agents to clean unrelated DAD work.

lesson_candidate.pattern: Before long Python/Rust validation verdicts, route temp/cache/target directories to writable repo-local ignored paths and classify access denied separately from code failures.
lesson_candidate.use_when: A repo runs pytest, validate_all, cargo test, Rust fast validators, scanners, or other long deterministic gates under a sandboxed coding agent.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: The failure contains deterministic assertion output or schema diagnostics after writable routing and unsandboxed reproduction, in which case it is a real code/data failure.

subject: T457 lesson candidate: scout-guided Rust canonical corpus QA leaf validator
summary: T457 used two read-only scout agents before implementation: a Rust architecture scout and a QA/governance scout. The scouts recommended avoiding dirty T423 chunking output and unmerged T451 edge taxonomy, then selected canonical corpus QA as the best immediate Rust slice because it is deterministic, high-volume, and structurally checkable. The branch turns the Rust canonical-qa scaffold into a real leaf validator with a Python wrapper, fallback, and compare mode.
extra_context: The owner wants many repos to grow Rust code where it makes sense and report reusable lessons to DAD. This report captures both the implementation asset and the process asset: use AI-agnostic scouts to pick Rust slices by fit, keep Rust on deterministic streaming checks, keep Python as governance orchestrator, and preserve non-authority boundaries. The QA scout also identified a future control-plane patch for vendor-neutral Rust subagent roles: rust_architecture_reviewer, outside_rust_research_scout, rust_engineer, rust_qa_tester, and dad_lesson_reporter.

lesson_candidate.pattern: Use scout agents to select Rust work by fit, then implement Rust as a deterministic leaf validator with Python fallback/compare governance wrapper.
lesson_candidate.use_when: A repo has high-volume JSONL/corpus/sidecar validation that is slow or runtime-sensitive, and there are multiple possible Rust tasks with different dependency risks.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: The work is theology policy, authority selection, chunk-quality judgment, graph truth, owner-gated promotion, or small YAML control-plane semantics.

subject: T458 lesson candidate: AI-agnostic Rust subagent charter with scout reporting
summary: T458 records a reusable pattern for Rust-heavy repo work: use capability-profile subagents for Rust architecture review, outside Rust research, bounded Rust implementation, Rust/Python QA, and DAD lesson reporting. The pattern keeps Python/pytest as governance orchestrator and reports scout findings as candidate-only DAD lessons.
extra_context: In the last few hours Logos Scripture Graph used read-only scout subagents while building Rust validator infrastructure. The architecture scout recommended five role types, capability-profile routing, no vendor/model lock-in, and validator assertions for Python/Rust parity and non-authority. The QA/DAD scout confirmed that DAD reporting should stay candidate-only with local lesson/context slots, extra_context for messy operating reality, and no attempt to clean unrelated DAD work. This is useful for DAD because many repos are rolling out Rust in parallel and will need a reusable way to coordinate architecture, outside examples, implementation, QA, and lesson reporting without dirtying central DAD state or making DAD authoritative.

lesson_candidate.pattern: Capability-profile Rust subagents with separate architecture, outside research, engineering, QA, and DAD-reporting roles
lesson_candidate.use_when: A repo is adding high-resource deterministic Rust scanners, validators, importers, chunk-map checkers, or other hot-path tooling that benefits from parallel agent review.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: The task is a small policy/YAML validator, semantic theology/chunking decision, reviewed-gold promotion, or any work where Rust speed would masquerade as correctness.
